fact: An adult's skin covers about 1.5 to 2 square metres.

text: Which planet is home to a giant storm called the Great Red Spot?
fact: The Great Red Spot is wider than Earth, though it has been slowly shrinking.

text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
fact: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.

text: How many hearts does an octopus have?
fact: Two hearts pump blood through the gills and the third pumps it around the body.

text: Which blood type is known as the universal donor for red cells?
fact: O negative red cells can be given to almost anyone, so hospitals keep them for emergencies.

text: Which is the longest bone in the human body?
fact: The femur is about a quarter of a person's height.

text: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
fact: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air. Oxygen is about 21%.

text: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
fact: Fleming noticed mould killing bacteria on a dish he had left out while on holiday.

text: Which part of the eye controls how much light gets in?
fact: The iris widens and narrows the pupil to control how much light reaches the retina.

text: Which vitamin does your skin make when exposed to sunlight?
fact: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for strong bones.

text: Which mineral sits at 10, the top of the Mohs hardness scale?
fact: German geologist Friedrich Mohs introduced his scratch-hardness scale in 1812.

text: Dry ice is the solid form of which substance?
fact: It's called dry ice because it never melts into a puddle. It turns straight into gas.

text: Botanically speaking, bamboo is a type of what?
fact: Some bamboo species can grow almost a metre in a single day.

text: What connects a muscle to a bone?
fact: Ligaments connect bone to bone. The Achilles is the body's thickest tendon.

text: What is a shark's skeleton made of?
fact: Shark cartilage is about half as dense as bone, which keeps the skeleton light.

text: Which planet is tipped over so far that it spins on its side?
fact: Uranus is tilted about 98 degrees, possibly after a huge collision long ago.

text: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
fact: The stapes, in the middle ear, is only about 2 to 3 mm long.

text: Which element has the chemical symbol K?
fact: K comes from kalium, the New Latin name for potassium.

text: What is the most abundant element in the universe?
fact: About three-quarters of all normal matter in the universe, by mass, is hydrogen.

text: Which of these metals is a liquid at 20°C?
fact: Gallium is close behind. It melts at about 30°C, so it can melt in your hand.

text: Which organ makes insulin?
fact: Insulin was first used to treat a diabetic patient in 1922, in Toronto.

text: Which is the fastest animal on Earth when diving?
fact: Peregrines hit their top speed in a hunting dive called a stoop.

text: Which gland in the neck makes hormones that control your metabolism?
fact: The butterfly-shaped thyroid sits at the front of the neck, just below the Adam's apple.

text: Which is the closest star to Earth after the Sun?
fact: Proxima Centauri is about 4.2 light years away, too faint to see without a telescope.

text: Marie Curie named which element after her home country?
fact: Poland didn't exist as an independent country when Curie named polonium in 1898.

text: In 1796, who used cowpox to protect a boy from smallpox?
fact: Jenner's name for cowpox, variolae vaccinae, gave us the word vaccine.

text: Which part of the brain mainly controls balance and coordination?
fact: The cerebellum is about 10% of the brain's volume but has more neurons than the rest combined.

text: What is the largest moon in the Solar System?
fact: Jupiter's moon Ganymede is wider than the planet Mercury.

text: Which planet has the fastest winds in the Solar System?
fact: Winds on Neptune reach about 2,000 km/h.

text: Which land animal has the longest pregnancy?
fact: An elephant pregnancy lasts about 22 months.

text: What will the Sun eventually become after its red giant phase?
fact: The Sun is too small to become a black hole or neutron star.

text: Aspirin was developed from a compound found in the bark of which tree?
fact: Willow remedies appear on clay tablets from ancient Sumer and in Egypt's Ebers Papyrus.

text: The tallest known living tree belongs to which species?
fact: A coast redwood in California named Hyperion is about 116 m tall.

text: Which planet is less dense than water?
fact: Saturn is the only planet in the Solar System whose average density is less than water's.

text: What chemical makes chilli peppers taste hot?
fact: Birds can't taste capsaicin, so they happily eat chillies and spread the seeds.

text: Barry Marshall drank a culture of which bacterium to prove it causes stomach ulcers?

text: Which device was pioneered by Australian surgeon Graeme Clark?

text: Which human cells have no nucleus when mature?

text: What was the first animal to orbit Earth?

text: What is the point in a planet's orbit closest to the Sun called?
fact: Earth reaches perihelion in early January, during the Australian summer.

text: Sound travels fastest through which of these?
fact: Sound moves through steel at about 5,900 m/s, roughly 17 times faster than in air.

text: Which element was discovered in the Sun before it was found on Earth?
fact: Helium is named after Helios, the Greek sun god.

text: What did Wilhelm Röntgen discover in 1895?
fact: One of his first X-ray photos showed his wife's hand, wedding ring and all.

text: Which part of a plant cell carries out photosynthesis?
fact: Chloroplasts descend from cyanobacteria that were taken in by an ancient cell.

text: Which SI unit is named after a Scottish inventor famous for steam engines?
fact: Watt also adopted horsepower as a unit to sell his steam engines.

text: What is the scientific study of fungi called?
fact: Phycology is the study of algae, and bryology the study of mosses.

text: The heart drug digitalis was first made from which plant?
fact: Foxglove is poisonous, but small doses of its compounds help a failing heart.

text: Which plant produces the largest single flower in the world?
fact: Rafflesia flowers can be a metre across and smell of rotting meat.

text: Four chemical elements are named after which Swedish village?
fact: Yttrium, ytterbium, terbium and erbium all take their names from Ytterby and its mine.

text: What does a dendrochronologist use to date events?
fact: Tree-ring records in some places reach back more than 10,000 years.

text: Which element is the best conductor of electricity?
fact: Silver beats copper, but copper is used in wiring because it's far cheaper.

text: Which scientist first identified hydrogen as a separate substance, in 1766?
fact: Cavendish called it "inflammable air". Lavoisier later named it hydrogen.

text: What is the lightest metal?
fact: Lithium is so light it floats on water, though it reacts with it as it does.

text: What word describes animals that are mostly active at dawn and dusk?
fact: Wallabies are among the many familiar mammals that are crepuscular.

text: Which blood vessel carries blood from the heart to the lungs?
fact: Unlike most arteries, it carries oxygen-poor blood, from the right side of the heart.

text: What is the most abundant element in Earth's crust?
fact: Oxygen makes up nearly half the crust by mass, mostly locked up in rocks.

fact: Thomson's son George later won a Nobel Prize for showing electrons also behave like waves.

text: Which metal has the highest melting point?
fact: Tungsten melts at about 3,400°C, which is why it was used in light bulb filaments.

text: Which chicken-sized bird lays an egg about six times the size of a hen's egg?
fact: A brown kiwi's egg can weigh as much as 450 g.

text: Which planet takes longer to spin once on its axis than to orbit the Sun?
fact: Venus spins once every 243 Earth days but orbits the Sun in 225.

text: The Mekong River reaches the sea in which country?
fact: The Mekong begins on the Tibetan Plateau and passes through six countries.

text: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
fact: Lesotho's lowest point is about 1,400 m above sea level, the highest low point of any country.

text: Lake Titicaca sits on the border of Peru and which other country?
fact: At about 3,800 m, Titicaca is one of the highest navigable lakes in the world.

text: The Matterhorn sits on the border between Switzerland and which country?
fact: The Matterhorn was first climbed in 1865. Four of the seven climbers died on the way down.

text: The desert city of Timbuktu is in which country?
fact: Timbuktu's mud-brick mosques date back to the 1300s.

text: Which European capital is built on the Vltava River?
fact: Prague's Charles Bridge over the Vltava was begun in 1357.

text: Which country's flag is made of two stacked triangles?
fact: Nepal's is the only national flag that is not a rectangle.

text: What is the deepest lake in the world?
fact: Lake Baikal in Siberia is over 1,600 m deep and holds over a fifth of Earth's fresh surface water.

text: Angel Falls, the highest uninterrupted waterfall on Earth, is in which country?
fact: Angel Falls is 979 m tall in total, with an unbroken drop of 807 m.

text: What is the capital of Morocco?
fact: Casablanca has Morocco's biggest metro area, but the king and parliament sit in Rabat.

text: Which country has three capital cities?
fact: Pretoria is the administrative capital, Cape Town the legislative and Bloemfontein the judicial.

text: The Equator passes through which of these countries?
fact: The Equator crosses the land of 11 countries, including Brazil, Indonesia and Ecuador.

text: Easter Island and its giant moai statues belong to which country?
fact: Easter Island is about 3,500 km from mainland Chile.

text: What is the northernmost capital city of an independent country?
fact: Nuuk is slightly further north, but Greenland is not an independent country.

text: What is the southernmost capital city of an independent country?
fact: Wellington lies at about 41 degrees south, roughly 6 degrees further south than Canberra.

text: What is the capital of Nigeria?
fact: Abuja was built as a planned city and replaced Lagos as capital in 1991.

text: Which river flows through the centre of Florence?
fact: Florence's Ponte Vecchio, lined with shops, crosses the Arno.

text: What is the highest mountain in South America?
fact: Aconcagua in Argentina is the highest peak outside Asia, at about 6,960 m.

text: The Rhine reaches the North Sea in which country?
fact: The Rhine runs about 1,230 km before it empties into the North Sea.

text: Which country has the largest number of native Spanish speakers?
fact: Mexico has more than twice as many Spanish speakers as Spain.

text: What is the largest country in Africa by area?
fact: Algeria became Africa's largest country in 2011, when South Sudan split from Sudan.

text: The Faroe Islands are a self-governing part of which country?
fact: The Faroes have had home rule since 1948 and are not part of the European Union.

text: Apart from Vatican City, which country is entirely surrounded by Italy?
fact: San Marino covers about 61 square km. Its capital sits on top of Monte Titano.

text: What is the smallest independent country in South America by area?
fact: Dutch is Suriname's official language, a legacy of Dutch rule that ended in 1975.

text: After Greenland, what is the world's second-largest island?
fact: New Guinea is split between Papua New Guinea and Indonesia.

text: The Bosphorus links the Black Sea to which body of water?
fact: The Bosphorus is under 1 km wide at its narrowest point.

text: Which city replaced Yangon as the capital of Myanmar in 2005?
fact: Naypyidaw has a 20-lane boulevard that, like most of its roads, is largely empty.

text: What is the longest river that flows entirely within one country?
fact: The Yangtze runs about 6,300 km across China, from the Tibetan Plateau to Shanghai.

text: The Okavango Delta, an inland delta that never reaches the sea, is in which country?
fact: The Okavango drains into the Kalahari, where nearly all its water evaporates or feeds plants.

text: Ouagadougou is the capital of which country?
fact: Burkina Faso was called Upper Volta until 1984.

text: What is the capital of Bhutan?
fact: Thimphu sits between about 2,250 and 2,650 m above sea level.

text: Which country's national flag has a different design on the front and back?
fact: Paraguay's flag shows the national seal on the front and the treasury seal on the back.

text: The Blue Nile and White Nile meet in which capital city?
Which sea is the only one with no coastline at all?
fact: The Sargasso Sea in the Atlantic is bounded by ocean currents, not land.

text: After Vatican City, what is the world's smallest country by area?
fact: Monaco covers about 2 square km, smaller than Sydney's Centennial Parklands.

text: What is the largest country that lies entirely within Europe?
fact: Ukraine covers about 600,000 square km. Russia and France both have land outside Europe.

text: Tbilisi is the capital of which country?
fact: Tbilisi's name comes from the Old Georgian word for "warm", after its hot springs.

text: The island of Socotra, home of the dragon's blood tree, belongs to which country?
fact: More than a third of Socotra's plant species grow nowhere else on Earth.
